title: Following Him
english: Let us work as the palm trees of the Phoenicians and follow Him, giving thanks; and instead of whiteness, let us take upright, undefiled, and simple faith; and instead of sharpness, let us take the patient hope that pierces and slays every thought that seeks to take us captive from the knowledge of God; and instead of the sweetness of the palm tree, let us take the sweet love that is composed of the aforementioned faith, hope, and the rest, so that what was said may be fulfilled in us: 'The righteous will flourish like a palm tree; he will grow like a cedar in Lebanon' (Psalm 92:12).

Let us follow Him into the holy city and enter the temple with Him, so that He may overturn the tables of the money changers within us and drive away the demons selling doves, the deceptive thoughts flying around us...
translator_notes: The Greek text is a fragment, beginning mid-sentence and ending mid-sentence; the translation reflects this with '...' and is rendered literally as a fragment.
The sentence 'The righteous will flourish like a palm tree; he will grow like a cedar in Lebanon' is a quotation from Psalm 92:12.

title: Prayer for Spiritual Healing
english: …of all those buying and selling among us, and instead of a den of robbers, make us a holy temple, according to the ancient temple, where Christ dwells and walks, so that he may give light to our blind, make the deaf hear, the lame walk, and raise the dead with Lazarus—for where life dwells, there is resurrection—so that with Lazarus, and the crowds, and his disciples, and with infants and nursing babies, and with the holy angels, we may cry out, shouting: 'Hosanna in the highest; blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord' (Psalm 118:26; Matthew 21:9), Christ our Lord and God, the 'king of the ages' (Revelation 11:15); to him be glory, honor, and worship, together with the Father and the Holy Spirit, now and forever and to the ages of ages. Amen.
translator_notes: The Greek text is a fragment, beginning mid-sentence with πάντων τῶν πωλούντων ἐν ἡμῖν καὶ ἀγοραζόντων.
The number 6 at the end of the source text appears to be an editor's note or a page number, and has been omitted from the translation.
